st: Rinse [[3 cups]] rice, then soak it in warm salted water for [[30 minutes]]. Drain well before using.
Heat [[0.75 cup]] oil in a heavy pot over high heat until it shimmers. Add the onions and cook for 8 minutes until deep golden.
Add the lamb and brown on all sides, about 8 minutes.
Add the carrots in an even layer on top of the meat. Cook for 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until softened.
Add [[2 tsp]] cumin, [[2 tsp]] salt, the soaked chickpeas and [[4 cups]] boiling water. Press the whole garlic head in the center. Simmer on low for [[40 minutes]] until the lamb is tender.
Drain the rice and spread it evenly over the meat without stirring.
Pour in just enough hot water to cover the rice by about 1 inch. Cook on high until the water is absorbed.
Gather the rice into a mound and poke a few holes with a spoon handle. Cover and cook on very low heat for [[20 minutes]].
Mix gently, then spread on a platter with the lamb and garlic on top.
Mix [[3 cups]] flour with [[1 tsp]] salt, then add [[0.75 cup]] warm water and [[2 tbsp]] melted butter. Knead into a smooth dough, 5 minutes.
Cover the dough and rest it for [[30 minutes]].
Mix the lamb, onions, [[1 tsp]] cumin, [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and [[0.5 tsp]] salt for the filling.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Roll the dough very thin into a rectangle and brush with some of the remaining melted butter. Roll it up like a log, then cut into 12 slices.
Press each slice flat and roll into a 4 inch circle, keeping the swirl side up.
Put a spoonful of filling in the middle, then fold the edges to form a triangle or square and pinch tightly.
Place the samsa seam side down on a lined tray. Brush with egg yolk and sprinkle with [[2 tbsp]] sesame seeds.
Bake for [[35 minutes]] until deep golden and the lamb reaches 160°F (71°C).
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a large pot over high heat and brown the beef for 6 minutes.
Add the onion and carrots and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, [[2 tbsp]] tomato paste, [[1 tsp]] cumin, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and bell peppers, then pour in [[3 cups]] broth.
Cover and simmer on low for [[40 minutes]] until the beef is tender and the sauce is thick.
Boil the noodles in salted water according to the package, then drain.
Divide the noodles between bowls and ladle the beef and vegetable sauce on top.
Sprinkle with [[0.25 cup]] cilantro and serve hot.
Mix [[3 cups]] flour, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[1 cup]] warm water, then knead 8 minutes into a firm dough.
Cover the dough and rest it for [[30 minutes]].
Mix the lamb, onions, [[1 tsp]] cumin, [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and [[1 tsp]] salt for the filling.
Roll the dough very thin and cut into 4 inch squares.
Put a spoonful of filling in each square, then pinch the corners together over the center to make a closed bundle.
Grease a steamer basket with [[1 tbsp]] oil and arrange the manti without touching.
Steam over boiling water for [[40 minutes]] until the filling reaches 160°F (71°C).
Serve hot with [[1.5 cups]] yogurt and drizzle with [[3 tbsp]] melted butter.
Combine the lamb with the onion in a large bowl.
Add [[3 tbsp]] vinegar, [[2 tsp]] cumin, [[2 tsp]] coriander, [[2 tsp]] salt, [[1 tsp]] pepper and [[2 tbsp]] oil. Mix well with your hands.
Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least [[4 hours]], or overnight.
If using wooden skewers, soak them in water for 30 minutes.
Thread the lamb onto skewers, packing the pieces tightly.
Heat a grill to medium-high.
Grill the skewers for 10 to 12 minutes, turning often, until browned and cooked to 145°F (63°C) or more.
Serve with raw onion rings and [[1 tsp]] sumac sprinkled on top.
Stir [[2.25 tsp]] yeast and [[1 tsp]] sugar into [[1.25 cups]] warm milk and wait 10 minutes until foamy.
Mix [[4 cups]] flour with [[1.5 tsp]] salt, then add the yeast milk and [[2 tbsp]] oil.
Knead for 10 minutes until smooth and stretchy.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for [[60 minutes]] until doubled.
Heat the oven with a baking stone or heavy tray inside to 475°F (245°C).
Divide the dough into 4 balls and flatten each into a round, leaving the center thin and the edge thick.
Press the center with a fork many times, or a stamp if you have one.
Brush with egg and sprinkle with [[2 tbsp]] sesame and [[1 tbsp]] nigella seeds.
Bake one at a time for [[10 minutes]] until deep golden.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large pot and brown the lamb for 8 minutes.
Add [[8 cups]] water, the soaked chickpeas, [[2 tsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] pepper.
Bring to a boil, skim off the foam, then cover and simmer on low for [[60 minutes]].
Add the onions and carrots and simmer for [[15 minutes]].
Add the potatoes and tomatoes and cook another [[20 minutes]] until all are tender.
Taste and add salt as needed.
Ladle into bowls, with a piece of meat in each, and top with [[0.25 cup]] dill.
Slice the tomatoes as thin as you can and spread them on a platter.
Slice the onion into thin rings and soak in cold water for [[10 minutes]] to take away the sharpness.
Drain the onion well and pat dry.
Scatter the onion over the tomatoes.
Sprinkle with [[0.25 cup]] basil and the minced chili.
Season with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.25 tsp]] pepper.
Let stand for 5 minutes so the tomato juices flow, then serve beside plov or grilled meat.
Mix [[3 cups]] flour, one egg, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 cup]] warm water. Knead 8 minutes into a firm dough.
Cover and rest the dough for [[30 minutes]].
Mix the beef, onion, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper for the filling.
Roll the dough very thin and cut into 2 inch squares.
Put a small bit of filling in the middle of each square and fold into a triangle. Pinch the two far corners together to make a little ear shape.
Bring [[8 cups]] broth to a simmer in a large pot.
Add the dumplings and cook for [[10 minutes]] until they float and the beef is cooked to 160°F (71°C).
Ladle into bowls, then top with [[1 cup]] yogurt and [[0.25 cup]] dill.
